## GET /admin-api/kerberos

`getKerberosSettings`

**The KDC's own settings**

The `krb5.*` settings: the realm, the two raw ports, the clock skew and the deliberate clock OFFSET, the one password every user account shares, the names that stay unknown, the long-term keys behind krbtgt, `s2kparams`, and the two that decide whether a ticket presented at /authn/spnego may start a browser session.

MOST OF THEM ARE RESTART-ONLY, and one fact is why: the principal database — every long-term key in it — is built from these when the process starts, so a realm or a password changed at runtime would leave every existing ticket undecryptable by the service that issued it.

TWO OF THEM EXIST TO MAKE FAILURES REACHABLE. `krb5.unknownUsers` names the only principals that can produce `KDC_ERR_C_PRINCIPAL_UNKNOWN` — every other name gets an account — and `krb5.clockOffset` moves this KDC's idea of now so a client can be shown `KRB_AP_ERR_SKEW` without anybody touching a system clock.

AND A `status` MEMBER (#173): what the KDC does about pre-authentication in this realm — whether a password alone gets a ticket for a person who holds or must hold a second factor (`passwordAloneRefused`; product refuses it with KDC_ERR_POLICY after the password verified), whether RFC 6113 FAST is served (`fast`, with its armor types and factors), and the RFC 8129 indicator an OTP pre-authentication puts in a ticket (`otpIndicator`).

THERE IS NO POST BESIDE THIS ONE and that is not a gap: every form on the console page this mirrors posts `set-many` to /admin/config, so `POST /admin-api/config/set-many` is already the operation for it. One store, one action, two doors.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/kerberos` on the admin console.

The reply also carries `protocolEndpoints`: every endpoint of this family in the realm the call arrived in, as `{ name, methods, url }` (plus `route` for an HTTP endpoint, `transport` for a socket, and `registered: false` for a route the router no longer has).

Scope: `admin:read`.

**200**: What the page says, and the settings it draws — described rows carrying each value's source and whether it can be changed while the service runs.

## GET /admin-api/kerberos/claims

`getKerberosPacClaims`

**The claims a Kerberos ticket's PAC carries**

The `kerberos-pac` claim set — the claims this realm's KDC writes into PAC_CLIENT_CLAIMS_INFO ([MS-PAC] 2.11) while `krb5.pacClaims` is on — with each row's claim id, the four PAC claim types and the claims one person's next TGT would carry, built by the function the KDC calls.

A TGT carries this set, with the person's realm-wide roles under it as a string claim. A service ticket carries what its TGT carried, with the rows of the application whose krb5ServicePrincipalName names the service added and winning by name (that application's Configuration tab, `krb5ClaimsPac`). A claim id is `ad://ext/<name>:<hex>`, the hex derived from the name (`idFormat`). Nothing already issued changes.

The set's TICKED CATALOGUE (#498) is the other pages' `attributeCatalogue` (each row with the `pacClaimId` it becomes) and `sets[].attributes`: a ticked attribute is a string claim of every value on the person's entry, under the rows and the roles claim, which win by claim id. `preview.byLdap` is what each attribute would carry for the person.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/kerberos` on the admin console.

The reply also carries `protocolEndpoints`: every endpoint of this family in the realm the call arrived in, as `{ name, methods, url }` (plus `route` for an HTTP endpoint, `transport` for a socket, and `registered: false` for a route the router no longer has).

Scope: `admin:read`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `user` | query | string |  | Whose claims to preview: `preview.claims` is what their next TGT would carry. |

**200**: The PAC set, its claim ids, the setting and the preview.

## POST /admin-api/kerberos/claims/add

`addKerberosPacClaim`

**Add one claim to one set**

Every ticket of that kind issued from now on carries it; nothing already issued changes.

ADDITIVE ONLY. What the protocol puts in is never displaced — an ID Token's `sub`, a SAML 2.0 assertion's `name`, a WS-Federation assertion's whole identity claim list. There is NO reserved list here: those names are load-bearing in a JWT, and an assertion attribute called `exp` collides with nothing. An entry with no name, and two entries of one name, are still refused.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/kerberos#kerberos-tab-claims` on the admin console.

## POST /admin-api/kerberos/claims/add-attribute-claim

`addKerberosPacAttributeClaim`

**Add one claim carrying a directory attribute**

The claim's value is `attribute` on the entry of the person the ticket is about (#94) — any attribute, where the directory-attribute half of a set offers only the fixed catalogue, under the name given here. Only the directory, never an invented value: a person whose entry lacks it gets no such claim, and a lower layer of the same name still answers. `multi` carries every value. A secret, a binary value or an attribute this service keeps (sts*, hoba*, app*, pwd*) is refused. Removed by `remove`, by name. The same reserved names are refused as for `add`, and a directory write that moves the attribute sends CAEP token-claims-change to holders of live tokens.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/kerberos#kerberos-tab-claims` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

| `type` | one of `string`, `int64`, `uint64`, `boolean` |  | The PAC claim type each value becomes; a value that is not one leaves the claim out of the ticket. |

## POST /admin-api/kerberos/claims/attributes

`setKerberosPacClaimAttributes`

**Set which LDAP attributes one set carries**

The array REPLACES the selection for that set. An attribute not in the array is removed, which is how removal is expressed — there is no per-attribute remove, because the console's control is a table of checkboxes and an API that removed differently would be a second model of the same state.

A selected attribute becomes a STRING PAC claim named ad://ext/&lt;attribute>:&lt;hex>, carrying EVERY value on that person's entry under ou=users; an entry without it carries no claim — nothing is invented (#498). Unlike POST /admin-api/credential-claims/select this does NOT sweep the directory: the credential page writes the attributes it needs onto every entry, and doing it from here as well would mean two pages racing to populate one directory. Selecting an attribute nobody has an entry value for still produces a claim; it is generated, and `attributeReport` says so per claim.

An unknown attribute name refuses the WHOLE call rather than being skipped: the catalogue is fixed, so an unknown name is either a hand-written request that deserves an answer or a rename that left a caller behind. `attributeCatalogue` in the GET beside this is the list — and it is ONE catalogue for all four sets, so either GET answers it in full.

A TYPED claim of the same name WINS over one of these, and THE PROTOCOL'S OWN beats both — which is worth knowing before it is discovered on the wire. An ID Token always carries name, given_name, family_name, preferred_username and email built from the sign-in, so selecting cn, givenName, sn, uid or mail ON THAT SET changes nothing the client sees; the same five reach an access token from the directory, because the protocol sets none of them there. A SAML 2.0 assertion sets `name` the same way and a WS-Federation one sets the whole identity claim list. Both halves are reported by that same GET.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/kerberos#kerberos-tab-claims` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `attributes` | list | yes | LDAP attribute type names, from `attributeCatalogue`. An EMPTY array clears the selection — and so does an ABSENT one, so a misspelt field name empties the set rather than being refused. The reply names everything it `removed` and the audit log keeps a row saying the same, and `attributes-clear` is how a caller that means it says so. |
| `attributes[]` | string |  |  |
| `set` | one of `kerberos-pac` | yes |  |

**200**: What the set carries now, in `attributes`, with `added` and `removed`.

**Set a whole claim set at once**

The array replaces whatever the set held. An EMPTY array is a legitimate call and clears it. Every entry is checked by the same rules `add` applies, and a single bad entry refuses the whole call — a partial replace would leave the set in a state nobody asked for.

| `claims[].attribute` | string |  | AN ATTRIBUTE CLAIM (#94), in place of `value`: the directory attribute of the person the artifact is about that the claim carries. Only the directory, never an invented value; absent on the entry, the claim is absent. A secret, a binary value or an attribute this service keeps (sts*, hoba*, app*, pwd*) is refused. |
| `claims[].multi` | boolean |  | An attribute claim: every value (a JSON array; several AttributeValues) rather than the first. |

| `claims[].nameFormat` | string |  |  |
| `claims[].namespace` | string |  |  |
| `claims[].type` | one of `string`, `number`, `boolean`, `json`, `int64`, `uint64` |  | An attribute claim in a JWT or UserInfo set: the JSON type each value becomes (string, number, boolean, json). A value that is not one is left out. Ignored by the SAML sets. In the Kerberos PAC set (#493) EVERY row has one, of string, int64, uint64 and boolean — the PAC claim type. |
| `claims[].value` | string |  | May carry a placeholder such as ${username}; `GET /admin-api/claims` lists the ones this service expands. |

## GET /admin-api/kerberos/principals

`getKerberosPrincipals`

**Who the KDC holds a stored long-term key for**

Three lists, paged separately with `?peoplePage=`, `?servicesPage=` and `?databasePage=` and one `?per=`.

`people` — the directory people whose Kerberos keys were derived from their own password when it was set or verified (PRODUCT MODE): the principal, the kvno, the enctypes, when and on what event the keys were derived, whether they are sealed, and `current` — whether they still match the password the entry holds. A person whose keys are not current is refused by the KDC until their next verified sign-in derives new ones.

`services` — the service principals created with a RANDOM key: the principal, the kvno, the enctypes, when created and last rotated.

`krbtgt` (#169) — the realm's krbtgt key: where it comes from (`stored`, `password` in development, `none`, `unreadable`), its kvno and enctypes, when it was made and last rotated, the versions kept and until when, and the schedule — `scheduled`, `offReason`, `intervalDays`, `nextDueAt`.

`database` (#595) — every principal the KDC holds, the development fixtures and the names created on first sight among them: the principal, its name type, salt, enctypes and kvno, and its flags, with `fixtureAccounts` and `realmsServed` beside it. What the demonstration document `GET /krb5/principals` listed until #595 deleted it, without its two development passwords.

**NO KEY MATERIAL IS IN THIS REPLY**, sealed or otherwise — both lists are built from the public info attributes. A trust realm has a KDC and a principal database of its own since 2026-09-15, so a realm prefix answers that realm's principals.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/kerberos` on the admin console.

The reply also carries `protocolEndpoints`: every endpoint of this family in the realm the call arrived in, as `{ name, methods, url }` (plus `route` for an HTTP endpoint, `transport` for a socket, and `registered: false` for a route the router no longer has).

Scope: `admin:read`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `per` | query | integer |  | Rows per page. Defaults to 50 and is capped at 300. On a drill-down it is SHARED by every list in the reply, which each carry a page number of their own. |
| `peoplePage` | query | integer |  | Which page of `people` to return, answered by `peoplePaging`. Directory people holding keys derived from their own password. |
| `servicesPage` | query | integer |  | Which page of `services` to return, answered by `servicesPaging`. Service principals created with a random key. |
| `databasePage` | query | integer |  | Which page of `database` to return, answered by `databasePaging`. Every principal in the KDC's database, by its public fields. |

**200**: The three lists with their paging, whether this is a product KDC, whether krb5.personKeys is on, the enctypes and starting kvno, and the acceptor's SPN.

## POST /admin-api/kerberos/principals/clear-person-keys

`clearKerberosPersonKeys`

**Clear a directory person's Kerberos keys**

Removes the Kerberos keys derived from `username`'s password. Their next AS-REQ is refused with "sign in once"; their next verified sign-in derives new keys at the next kvno. Somebody with no keys answers `cleared: false` rather than a refusal, so a script may clear on every run. There is no operation that SETS a person's keys: they come from the person's password and from nothing else.

## POST /admin-api/kerberos/principals/create-service

`createKerberosServicePrincipal`

**Create a service principal with a random key, and get its keytab once**

Makes a RANDOM key for every enctype in `krb5.enctypes` (never rc4-hmac in product mode), at kvno `krb5.kvno`, for `spn` in this KDC's realm, stores them SEALED on the application entry for `<spn>@<realm>` (creating that entry if it is not there), and answers with an MIT keytab (format 0x502) in `keytab`, base64.

**THE KEYTAB IS IN THIS REPLY AND NOWHERE ELSE**: it cannot be downloaded again. A lost one is replaced by `rotate-service`.

The KDC issues tickets for that SPN under the stored key from the next request, in both modes, and this service's own acceptor prefers it when the SPN is `krb5.servicePrincipal`. Refused for an SPN that already holds a stored key, for `krbtgt/*`, for another realm, and for anything that is not two or more `/`-separated components.

## POST /admin-api/kerberos/principals/reset-person-keytab

`resetKerberosPersonKeytab`

**Reset a person's password, and get the keytab derived from it once**

SETS `username`'s password — to `password`, or with `random: true` to a generated one that is NEVER returned — and answers with an MIT keytab (format 0x502) in `keytab`, base64, derived from it: one entry per enctype in `krb5.enctypes` (never rc4-hmac in product mode), at the CURRENT kvno only.

**THIS IS A PASSWORD RESET.** A stored key is never read back out, so a keytab is derived from a password in hand, and the only one an administrator can have is one set now. The old password stops working in every protocol, the kvno moves up by one, an outstanding reset link is spent, the person is signed out of everything, and a CAEP credential-change is sent. They are NOT made to change it at their next sign-in (that would end the keytab), and a pending forced change is cleared.

The password is held to the realm's password policy. The key derived from it is checked against the one the KDC holds before the keytab is returned. In DEVELOPMENT mode the KDC keys every user from `krb5.userPassword`, not from their own, so the keytab is derived from that — `source` says which. **THE KEYTAB IS IN THIS REPLY AND NOWHERE ELSE.** Refused, before anything changes, for a realm with no KDC, a name with no entry, a disabled account, and `krb5.personKeys` off in product mode; and for neither or both of `password` and `random`. The person makes their own, from their own password and with nothing reset, at `/portal/kerberos`.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/kerberos#kerberos-tab-principals, POST /admin/kerberos/principals` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `password` | string |  | The new password. Leave out with `random`. |
| `random` | boolean |  | A generated password under the password policy, never returned. |
| `username` | string | yes | The person, as they sign in, in the trust realm of the call. |

**200**: The principal, kvno, enctypes, `source` (`password` or `development`), whether the password was generated, the sign-out, and the keytab (base64) with a file name for it.

| `keytabFilename` | string |  |  |

| `kvno` | number |  |  |
| `message` | string |  |  |
| `ok` | boolean | yes |  |

## POST /admin-api/kerberos/principals/rotate-krbtgt

`rotateKerberosKrbtgt`

**Rotate the realm's krbtgt key, keeping the one it replaces for the TGTs already sealed under it**

Queues a run of the scheduler job `krb5.krbtgt-rotate-now` for the trust realm of the call, which runs once, on the scheduler's leader, at its next tick: a new RANDOM key for every enctype in `krb5.enctypes`, at the next kvno, sealed on the directory entry `krbtgt/<REALM>@<REALM>`. The key it replaces is KEPT — at most `krb5.retainedKeyVersions`, for the longer of the ticket and renew lifetimes plus the clock skew unless `krb5.retainedKeyTtlS` names a number — so every TGT already issued goes on working until it expires. In development mode it replaces the key derived from `krb5.krbtgtPassword`, which is then the version kept.

**NO KEY IS IN THE REPLY, OR ANYWHERE.** The answer is the run's id; `GET /admin-api/kerberos/principals` shows the `krbtgt` block with its new kvno once the run has happened. Refused in a realm with no KDC.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/kerberos#kerberos-tab-principals, POST /admin/kerberos/principals` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Request body** (optional)

An empty object.

**200**: `queued`, the `runId`, and whether an identical run was already queued.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |

| `alreadyQueued` | boolean |  |  |
| `errors` | list |  |  |
| `errors[]` | string |  |  |
| `invalidate` | boolean |  |  |
| `message` | string |  |  |
| `ok` | boolean | yes |  |
| `queued` | boolean |  |  |
| `runId` | number, or string |  |  |
| `trustRealm` | string, or null |  |  |

**400**: The operation was refused; `errors` says why and nothing changed.

`rotateKerberosKrbtgtInvalidate`

**Rotate the realm's krbtgt key and keep NOTHING, so every TGT in the realm is refused**

Active Directory's double reset in one act, for a krbtgt key presumed compromised: `rotate-krbtgt` with no previous version kept, so every TGT the realm issued before the run is refused KRB_AP_ERR_BADKEYVER at its next TGS-REQ and every person runs a fresh AS exchange. ## POST /admin-api/kerberos/principals/rotate-service

`rotateKerberosServicePrincipal`

**Replace a service principal's key, and get the new keytab once**

New random keys at the stored kvno PLUS ONE, and the new keytab in `keytab`, base64.

**THE VERSION IT REPLACES IS KEPT** — at most `krb5.retainedKeyVersions` previous versions, each for `krb5.retainedKeyTtlS` (by default the ticket lifetime plus the clock skew) — and **the keytab carries them too**, as MIT's `ktadd` leaves one: `keytabKvnos` lists every version in it and `retained` says until when each is accepted. A ticket already issued under a kept version is still accepted by this KDC and its acceptor; nothing new is issued under it, and past its window it is refused KRB_AP_ERR_BADKEYVER. `drop-previous-service-keys` ends the window at once. Refused for an SPN with no stored key.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/kerberos#kerberos-tab-principals, POST /admin/kerberos/principals` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

## GET /admin-api/kerberos/trusts

`getKerberosTrusts`

**The realm's Kerberos trusts, with their keys described and never carried**

The trust records of the realm the call is in, paged with `?trustsPage=` and `?per=`, and one record whole with `?trust=<partner realm>` (`trust`, or `unknownTrust` naming a partner this realm holds no trust with).

Each row: the partner realm, NetBIOS name and domain SID, the type (`external`, `trust-realm`), the direction, the [MS-ADTS] 6.1.6.7.9 attributes by name and as the `trustAttributes` mask, the [MS-PAC] 4.1.2.2 boundary, the routed DNS suffixes, the enctypes, the forest trust information and claims transformation, and per key (`incoming`, `outgoing`) whether it is held, its kvno, its source and when it was set — the incoming side with the PREVIOUS version a rotation keeps and until when it is accepted. `health` lists the findings the console's health column draws (`kind`, `level`, `text`).

`form` is what the add and edit forms are drawn from: the closed attribute set with its contradictions and requirements, the types, directions, key sources, enctypes, claims transformations, the shortest trust password, and the other trust realms a `trust-realm` partner may name. `settings` are the four the trusts read. **NO KEY MATERIAL IS IN THIS REPLY.**

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/kerberos` on the admin console.

The reply also carries `protocolEndpoints`: every endpoint of this family in the realm the call arrived in, as `{ name, methods, url }` (plus `route` for an HTTP endpoint, `transport` for a socket, and `registered: false` for a route the router no longer has).

Scope: `admin:read`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `per` | query | integer |  | Rows per page. Defaults to 50 and is capped at 300. On a drill-down it is SHARED by every list in the reply, which each carry a page number of their own. |
| `trustsPage` | query | integer |  | Which page of `trusts` to return, answered by `trustsPaging`. The realm's trust records. |
| `trust` | query | string |  | One partner realm, for its record whole. |

**200**: The trust records with their paging and health, the drill-down record, what the forms are drawn from, and the trust settings.

## POST /admin-api/kerberos/trusts/add

`addKerberosTrust`

**Add a trust with another Kerberos realm**

Writes a trust record in this realm's directory (`ou=kerberosTrusts`) for `partnerRealm`. `direction` decides which keys it holds — `inbound` the incoming `krbtgt/<us>@<partner>` (the partner's tickets are accepted), `outbound` the outgoing `krbtgt/<partner>@<us>` (this realm refers to the partner), `bidirectional` both — and `keySource` where each comes from: `password`, a shared trust password both KDCs derive the key from (RFC 3961 string-to-key, RFC 4120's default salt), written and never shown back; or `generate`, random keys returned ONCE in `shown`. `attributes` are [MS-ADTS] 6.1.6.7.9's bits by name (`quarantined` by default); a contradiction or a missing requirement is refused. `forestTrustInfo` belongs to a cross-forest trust only. Refused for this realm's own name, a partner already held, and every field out of shape, each with its own code.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/kerberos#kerberos-tab-trusts, POST /admin/kerberos/trusts` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `attributes` | list |  | [MS-ADTS] 6.1.6.7.9's bits by name. |
| `attributes[]` | string |  |  |
| `attributesShown` | string |  | Set by the console's form: the attribute boxes were drawn. |
| `claimsTransformation` | one of `drop-all`, `allow-all` |  | What becomes of a claims set arriving across it. |
| `direction` | one of `bidirectional`, `inbound`, `outbound` |  | Which keys the record holds. |
| `enabled` | boolean |  | Whether it is used; true by default. |
| `enctypes` | list |  | The enctypes its keys are made for, by number; AES by default. |
| `enctypes[]` | integer or string |  |  |
| `forestDomains` | string |  | The form's text: a domain per line, `<sid> <dns name> <netbios name> [disabled]`. |
| `forestNames` | string |  | The form's text: a top-level name per line, `<name> [disabled]`. |
| `forestTrustInfo` | object or string, or null |  | A cross-forest trust's { domains: [{ sid, dnsName, netbiosName, sidEnabled }], topLevelNames: [{ name, enabled }] }. |
| `keySource` | one of `password`, `generate` |  | Where a key it does not hold yet comes from. |
| `netbiosName` | string |  | Its NetBIOS (flat) name; the realm's first label by default. |
| `partnerRealm` | string | yes | The partner Kerberos realm, PARTNER.EXAMPLE. |
| `partnerSid` | string |  | Its domain SID, S-1-5-21-a-b-c; a trust realm's own by default. |
| `partnerTrustRealm` | string |  | For `trust-realm`: that trust realm's id. |
| `password` | string |  | The shared trust password, for `keySource: "password"`. Never shown back. |
| `suffixes` | list |  | The DNS suffixes routed to the partner. |
| `suffixes[]` | string |  |  |
| `type` | one of `external`, `trust-realm` |  | `external` — a KDC elsewhere — or `trust-realm`, another trust realm of this service. |

## POST /admin-api/kerberos/trusts/disable

`disableKerberosTrust`

**Turn a trust off, keeping its keys**

A disabled trust refers nobody and accepts no ticket (`STS-KRB-0229`); its keys are kept, so `enable` restores it as it was.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/kerberos#kerberos-tab-trusts, POST /admin/kerberos/trusts` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `partnerRealm` | string | yes | The partner Kerberos realm. |

## POST /admin-api/kerberos/trusts/enable

`enableKerberosTrust`

**Turn a trust on**

The record for `partnerRealm` refers and accepts again, with the keys it kept.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/kerberos#kerberos-tab-trusts, POST /admin/kerberos/trusts` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `partnerRealm` | string | yes | The partner Kerberos realm. |

## POST /admin-api/kerberos/trusts/pair

`pairKerberosTrust`

**Write the matching record on the partner trust realm**

For a record whose partner is another trust realm of this service (`partnerRealm`), writes that realm's record for this one in the same act — its incoming key this realm's outgoing and the other way round, the same attributes and enctypes — or, where it already holds one, makes its keys match. With `otherRealm` (a trust realm's id) instead, writes BOTH records from nothing, from one password or one generated key set. Either way it writes another realm's directory, so it is a service administrator's act.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/kerberos#kerberos-tab-trusts, POST /admin/kerberos/trusts` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `attributes` | list |  | With `otherRealm`. |
| `attributes[]` | string |  |  |
| `direction` | one of `bidirectional`, `inbound`, `outbound` |  | With `otherRealm`: the keys, from this realm's side. |
| `enctypes` | list |  | With `otherRealm`. |
| `enctypes[]` | integer or string |  |  |
| `keySource` | one of `password`, `generate` |  | With `otherRealm`. |
| `otherRealm` | string |  | A trust realm's id, to pair from nothing. |
| `partnerRealm` | string |  | A record held here, to mirror. |
| `partnerSuffixes` | list |  | With `otherRealm`: what the other routes here. |
| `partnerSuffixes[]` | string |  |  |
| `password` | string |  | With `keySource: "password"`. |
| `suffixes` | list |  | With `otherRealm`: what this realm routes to the other. |
| `suffixes[]` | string |  |  |

**200**: Both records' views, whether the other was created or matched, and a generated key once in `shown`.

## POST /admin-api/kerberos/trusts/remove

`removeKerberosTrust`

**Remove a trust and its keys**

Deletes the record for `partnerRealm`, keys and all: no referral is made through it and no ticket is accepted from it, at once. Confirmed by `confirm` repeating the partner realm (`STS-ADMIN-0860` otherwise). `disable` keeps the keys instead.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/kerberos#kerberos-tab-trusts, POST /admin/kerberos/trusts` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `confirm` | string | yes | The partner realm again. |
| `partnerRealm` | string | yes | The partner Kerberos realm. |

**200**: Whether it was removed.

## POST /admin-api/kerberos/trusts/rotate-key

`rotateKerberosTrustKey`

**Replace a trust's keys at the next kvno, keeping the incoming one for a grace**

New keys for `side` (`both`, the default, `incoming` or `outgoing`, of the sides held) at the current kvno plus one, from `keySource`. The incoming version it replaces still opens the partner's tickets for `krb5.trustKeyGraceSeconds` (by default the ticket lifetime plus the clock skew) and is refused KRB_AP_ERR_BADKEYVER after it. With `mirror: true` and a `trust-realm` partner, that realm's record is rotated in the same act the other way round — a service administrator's act. Without it the partner's administrator gives their side the same password or the keys in `shown`.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/kerberos#kerberos-tab-trusts, POST /admin/kerberos/trusts` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `keySource` | one of `password`, `generate` | yes | Where the new key comes from. |
| `mirror` | boolean |  | Rotate the partner trust realm's record too. |
| `partnerRealm` | string | yes | The partner Kerberos realm. |
| `password` | string |  | The new trust password, for `keySource: "password"`. |
| `side` | one of `both`, `incoming`, `outgoing` |  | Which keys. |

**200**: The record's view, the sides rotated, the partner realm's record when mirrored, and a generated key once in `shown`.

## POST /admin-api/kerberos/trusts/update

`updateKerberosTrust`

**Change a trust's fields**

Changes the record for `partnerRealm`: a field not given keeps its value. A key already held keeps its key — `rotate-key` changes one — and a `direction` that adds a side takes `keySource` for it, one that drops a side removes that key. The partner realm cannot change: every key is salted with it.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/kerberos#kerberos-tab-trusts, POST /admin/kerberos/trusts` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `attributes` | list |  | [MS-ADTS] 6.1.6.7.9's bits by name. |
| `attributes[]` | string |  |  |
| `attributesShown` | string |  | Set by the console's form: the attribute boxes were drawn. |
| `claimsTransformation` | one of `drop-all`, `allow-all` |  | What becomes of a claims set arriving across it. |
| `direction` | one of `bidirectional`, `inbound`, `outbound` |  | Which keys the record holds. |
| `enabled` | boolean |  | Whether it is used; true by default. |
| `enctypes` | list |  | The enctypes its keys are made for, by number; AES by default. |
| `enctypes[]` | integer or string |  |  |
| `forestDomains` | string |  | The form's text: a domain per line, `<sid> <dns name> <netbios name> [disabled]`. |
| `forestNames` | string |  | The form's text: a top-level name per line, `<name> [disabled]`. |
| `forestTrustInfo` | object or string, or null |  | A cross-forest trust's { domains: [{ sid, dnsName, netbiosName, sidEnabled }], topLevelNames: [{ name, enabled }] }. |
| `keySource` | one of `password`, `generate` |  | Where a key it does not hold yet comes from. |
| `netbiosName` | string |  | Its NetBIOS (flat) name; the realm's first label by default. |
| `partnerRealm` | string | yes | The partner Kerberos realm, PARTNER.EXAMPLE. |
| `partnerSid` | string |  | Its domain SID, S-1-5-21-a-b-c; a trust realm's own by default. |
| `partnerTrustRealm` | string |  | For `trust-realm`: that trust realm's id. |
| `password` | string |  | The shared trust password, for `keySource: "password"`. Never shown back. |
| `suffixes` | list |  | The DNS suffixes routed to the partner. |
| `suffixes[]` | string |  |  |
| `type` | one of `external`, `trust-realm` |  | `external` — a KDC elsewhere — or `trust-realm`, another trust realm of this service. |
